observations.explanation: The paper describes adding reflections to working memory before resetting and trying again (PDF pp. 3–4), and explicitly constrains the agent to binary success/failure feedback (p. 4). Its discussion also presents the approach as broadly applicable, so “potentially” is appropriately qualified (pp. 7, 10).

The evaluation covers 134 AlfWorld environments, and reports solving 97% in 12 trials (PDF p. 5). The authors explicitly characterize the comparison as improved accuracy through self-improved learning rather than success by retry (p. 5).

The HotPotQA evaluation used 100 questions (PDF p. 6). The paper reports improvement over the baseline across trials, but this test size does not itself establish generalization to broader datasets; the assessment appropriately describes that as unestablished rather than as a demonstrated failure (pp. 6–7).

The paper reports only small WebShop gains after four trials and says the agent did not show helpful, intuitive reflections (PDF p. 10). It also notes that successful purchase outcomes may depend on search-engine result quality, which reflection cannot fully address (p. 10).
